title: Scaling Safely: Vertical vs Horizontal
objectives: Master the 20% rule for safe vertical budget scaling
Implement horizontal scaling by expanding audiences and creative angles
Know when to duplicate winning campaigns versus scaling in-place

blocks.text: Scaling is the ultimate test of a media buyer! Here is how you multiply ad spend without blowing up your costs.
There are two fundamental ways to scale Meta campaigns: Vertical Scaling (budget) and Horizontal Scaling (audience and creative breadth).

left.title: Vertical Scaling
points: Increase budget on an existing winning ad set
The 20% Rule: Increase budget by max 15-20% every 48-72 hours

right.title: Horizontal Scaling
points: Scale by finding new audiences and creative angles
Test 2% Lookalike, Broad Demographics, or new cities
Duplicate winning ad sets into new targets

blocks.title: The Airplane Engine Analogy
blocks.text: If a pilot pushes the throttle from 20% to 100% in half a second, the engine stalls. If they smoothly advance the throttle in calibrated increments, the plane soars safely into the sky!

When to Duplicate: If an ad set is performing at 4.0x ROAS with ₹1,000/day and you want to test aggressive budget jumps (e.g. ₹5,000/day), duplicate it into a separate campaign so you never risk breaking the original winner.
Never double a winning ad set's budget overnight (e.g. ₹2,000 to ₹4,000). It shocks the bidding algorithm and immediately sends it back to Learning Phase.

quiz.q: What is the recommended maximum percentage budget increase when vertically scaling an ad set in-place?
options: Up to 15% to 20% every 48 to 72 hours
quiz.explain: Increments under 20% keep the bidding model calibrated without resetting machine learning.

quiz.q: What is 'Horizontal Scaling' in Meta media buying?
options: Expanding reach by testing new creative angles, new lookalike tiers, and broader geographic audiences
Running ads only between 9 AM and 5 PM
quiz.explain: Horizontal scaling expands the total pool of addressable prospects by adding new angles and audiences.

quiz.q: Why is duplicating a winning ad set into a new campaign with a higher budget often safer than editing the original?
options: It protects the original profitable baseline from breaking if the high-budget test fails to stabilize
Meta gives free bonus ad spend for duplicated ads
quiz.explain: Duplication preserves the steady baseline cash flow while isolating high-budget experimentation.

quiz.q: True or False: If you increase budget by 200% in one click, Meta guarantees that your lead volume will triple.
quiz.explain: False! Sudden budget shocks typically degrade auction efficiency, causing CPL to double or triple instead.

recap: Scale vertically using the 20% rule every 48-72 hours to preserve machine learning.
Scale horizontally by discovering new creative angles and expanding to broad targeting.
